quote: the help of the tanks of "B" Squadron of the 6th Armoured Regiment was invaluable
note: D.D. tanks landed on the Courseulles beaches (Mike sector) with 7th Brigade; B Sqn helped the Reginas at the East Courseulles strongpoint

quote: Assistance was asked from the 6th Armoured Regiment
note: Advance held up by machine-gun fire in front of Ste. Croix; tanks beat down the opposition

quote: through Camilly to the north edge of Secqueville-en-Bessin
note: Only one troop of C Sqn (Lt. W. F. McCormick), which then turned back; furthest point reached, not where the regiment was

quote: the whole of the 6th Armoured Regiment harboured at Pierrepont
note: Night harbour of 6/7 June, in the 7th Brigade area (planned harbour had been Beny-sur-Mer--Basly)

quote: with "B" Squadron supporting the Queen's Own
note: D.D. tanks in the assault on Nan White, Bernières, with the Queen's Own Rifles
C Sqn with the North Shore Regiment at St. Aubin; the text names the regiment but not the beach for each squadron, the place follows the battalion

quote: pushed southward towards Beny-sur-Mer, supported by "A" Squadron
note: A Sqn with the advance from Bernières south toward Bény-sur-Mer; regiment's night position not given

quote: had run into other resistance at Villons-les-Buissons
note: Advanced guard of 9th Brigade with the North Nova Scotia Highlanders from 6:20 p.m., via Colomby-sur-Thaon

quote: The infantry and tanks accordingly formed a fortress
note: Night of 6/7 June, dug in with the North Novas in the area Anisy--Villons-les-Buissons

quote: the commanders of the 8th and 9th Infantry Brigades and the 2nd Armoured Brigade
note: Only the brigade commander is placed: at General Keller's 2:35 p.m. conference at 3rd Division HQ, Bernières. Brigade HQ location not given
